newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says people more important than profit.
newsitem.headline: Pope says people more important than profit.

text.p: Pope John Paul criticised unbridled free market economics on Friday, telling an audience of distinguished academics and bankers that people were more important than profit.
In a written address to a meeting of the Pontifical Academy of Social Sciences, the leader of the world's Roman Catholics said the Church was not against free market economics as such.

But he told an audience which included Hans Tietmeyer, chairman of Germany's Bundesbank (central bank), that economic systems had to serve the "primacy of the human person" and that every man had a "primordial right to work".

"History broadly shows the failure of regimes marked by planning which injures civil and economic freedoms," the Pope, 76, said in a reference to the communist system that collapsed in his native Poland and elsewhere in Eastern Europe.
"But that does not of itself lend credit to systems that are diametrically opposite," the Pope added.
"Unfortunately, experience illustrates that a market economy, left to unconditional freedom, is far from bringing the greatest possible advantage to people and societies," he said.
The Pope, who met the group before leaving on a visit to the Czech Republic, said rapid economic growth in newly industrialised countries created wealth but also carried a human price.
He said it was essential that political action was aimed at creating a welfare system in the midst of market economies to protect the weakest sectors of society.
"There are still too many poor people around the world, who have no access to the least share of the opulent wealth of a minority," the Pope added.
The Pontifical Academy began a five-day meeting on Tuesday on the subject of work and is due to conclude on Saturday by drawing up a series of recommendations for the Vatican.
